records.assertion: Fittipaldi won the 1973 Brazilian GP (first championship Brazilian GP at Interlagos) and 1974; Pace won 1975.
records.notes: 'First championship Brazilian GP at Interlagos' rests on F1DB: race 222 (1973) is the earliest championship race at this circuit. 1974/1975 winners from F1DB only.

records.assertion: Before 1975 a Brazilian driver had already won at Interlagos.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence merges EN s1 and s2 (adds Fittipaldi 1973 first championship win and 1974 repeat); UK alignment is shifted by one sentence for s2-s6.
records.notes: Rhetorical sentence; implied fact (prior Brazilian win) holds via F1DB 1973/1974.

records.assertion: Fittipaldi won the first World Championship Brazilian GP at Interlagos in 1973 and won again in 1974.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence is about Pace in January 1975 (matches EN s3, not s2).
records.notes: 1974 win from F1DB only; 'first WC' from F1DB circuit ordering.

records.assertion: In January 1975 home crowd followed Brazilian Carlos Pace driving a Brabham.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence describes Jarier's Shadow and lap-32 fuel failure (EN s4 content).
records.notes: Date 26 Jan 1975 confirmed by F1DB and both sources.

records.assertion: Jarier's Shadow was fastest, pulled clear, and retired with fuel-system trouble on lap 32.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence says Pace took the lead with Fittipaldi closing (EN s5 content).
records.notes: Substance correct. Same source says lap 32 (narrative) and lap 33 (retirement list); F1.com shows 32 laps completed. Safer wording: 'after 32 laps'.

records.assertion: After Jarier's retirement Pace led, with Fittipaldi's McLaren closing on him.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence says Carlos held on and took his only F1 win (EN s6 content).

records.assertion: Pace won (his only F1 victory), Fittipaldi second, Mass third.
records.uk_issue: UK sentence gives only the podium (2nd/3rd); 'only victory' sits in UK s5 due to alignment shift.
records.notes: Podium verified by F1DB. Cited sources say 'first', not 'only'. Uncited FIA media kit (src-f471275d7099 p1) states 'the only victory of his career' — add that citation.

records.assertion: 1975 classification was a Brazilian one-two; Jarier had looked set to win.
records.uk_issue: UK omits Jarier and the crowd ending; says only that the day could have gone differently.
records.notes: Brazilian nationality of both from 'home crowd'/'home Grand Prix' passages.

records.assertion: After Jarier retired, Fittipaldi stayed close enough to Pace to make the finish a real contest.
records.notes: Source says Fittipaldi was catching but never got close enough; margin 5.79s. 'Real contest' overstates it; 'Fittipaldi was closing' would be supported.

records.assertion: Two Brazilians on the podium: reigning champion Fittipaldi chasing, and Pace taking his only championship GP win.
records.uk_issue: UK says 'the only one of his career' (broader than EN 'only championship Grand Prix').
records.notes: Podium and champion status supported; 'only' not in cited sources (FIA media kit, uncited here, supports it).

records.assertion: Interlagos originated in plans for a resort between the Guarapiranga and Billings reservoirs.
records.notes: Cited page mentions neither a resort plan nor the reservoirs. Mercedes page (uncited here) names the two lakes but not a resort.

records.assertion: The circuit opened in 1940; F1 championship came in 1973 amid Fittipaldi's success.

evidence.locator: 'When was its first Grand Prix?' section

records.notes: 1973 and Fittipaldi context supported; source gives 1938 construction start only, no 1940 opening date. UK 'had already made' vs EN 'was making' is a slight nuance shift.

records.assertion: The long original layout was replaced by a much shorter one in 1990.
records.notes: Length change established by F1DB layouts.

records.assertion: The Senna S leads downhill to a winding infield and the lap climbs back to the start.
All of Fittipaldi's Interlagos wins came on the long (pre-1990) layout.
records.notes: F1DB: Fittipaldi wins 1973/1974 only, both on interlagos-1 (7.873 km). Second clause is evaluative.

records.assertion: Fittipaldi, driving for Lotus, won the first World Championship Brazilian GP at Interlagos.

evidence.locator: 'When was its first Grand Prix?' section
'When was its first Grand Prix?' section

records.notes: Win and 'first WC race' supported; 'for Lotus' not in the cited page. Lotus appears in uncited snapshots (F1.com 1973 result, FIA kit) — add a citation.

records.assertion: Fittipaldi won again in 1974 and Pace won in 1975: home wins in the first three championship races at the venue.

evidence.locator: 'When was its first Grand Prix?' section

records.assertion: In 1991 Senna's McLaren began losing gears while he was heading for victory.
Senna finished using sixth gear ahead of a closing Patrese, his first home GP win.
Turn 1 (S do Senna) is a left-hander dropping downhill from the pit straight.
records.notes: FIA map text gives only corner numbers; media kit has no corner descriptions. Mercedes page (uncited here) supports left-right downhill.

records.assertion: The Senna S was created in the 1990 redesign with Senna's input; T1 braking is the main overtaking spot.
records.notes: No cited source mentions the 1990 redesign or Senna's input. Historical claim needs a dedicated source.

records.assertion: Turn 2 is a right-hander immediately after the downhill Turn 1.
records.notes: FIA map text lacks corner directions; media kit irrelevant.

records.assertion: Late braking into T1 compromises T2 and the exit through Curva do Sol.
records.notes: Driving-technique description.

records.assertion: Turn 3 Curva do Sol ('Curve of the Sun') is a long left after the Senna S.
records.notes: Cited FIA documents carry no corner names. Mercedes page (uncited here) supports it.

records.assertion: A good T3 exit matters for slipstreaming on the Reta Oposta before braking for T4.
records.notes: Map lists DRS positions near T3/T4 but label-to-position mapping is unclear in extracted text; does not state the slipstream claim.

records.assertion: Turn 4 is a left at the end of Reta Oposta, starting Descida do Lago.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited here) supports Turns 4 & 5 as Descida do Lago left-handers.

records.assertion: Turn 4 is a major overtaking zone.
Turn 5 is the second left of Descida do Lago, continuing downhill before the road climbs to Ferradura.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited) says Descida do Lago starts at a low point heading upward and calls Ferradura 'two downhill right-handers' — elevation description may be wrong.

records.assertion: Descida do Lago refers to a lakeside descent; exit prepares for the faster right-hand section.
Ferradura means horseshoe, after the section's curved right-hand shape.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited here) supports the translation.

records.assertion: Turn 6 starts a faster sequence; drivers balance the car rather than chase one late apex.
Turn 7 continues the right-hand Ferradura with elevation change.
Smooth steering at T7 to prepare for the tighter infield is more valuable than sliding wide.
Turn 8 Laranjinha ('Little Orange') is a tighter right-hander in the middle sector.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited here) supports name and right-hander.

records.assertion: Origin of the Laranjinha name is disputed (editorial meta-statement).
records.notes: Sentence refers to 'the guide' itself; no source on competing explanations.

records.assertion: Turn 9 Pinheirinho ('Little Pine Tree') is a slow infield left.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited here) supports it.

records.assertion: A wide T9 exit compromises the very tight right-hand Bico de Pato.
Turn 10 Bico de Pato ('Duck's Bill') is a sharp right-hand hairpin.
records.notes: Mercedes page (uncited here) supports name/right-hander; 'hairpin' unsourced.

records.assertion: T10 is the slowest part of the middle sector; exit affects the left-hand Mergulho.
Turn 11 Mergulho ('Dive') is a downhill left before Junção.
records.notes: Mercedes (uncited) supports 'Dive' and downhill; direction not stated there.

records.assertion: Drivers must anticipate the slower left after the downhill T11.
Turn 12 Junção ('Junction') is the key slow left before the long uphill acceleration.
records.notes: FIA map only references T12 in DRS labels. Mercedes page (uncited here) supports name and criticality.

records.assertion: Junção exit traction determines speed onto the pit straight.
Turn 13 Curva do Café begins the uphill, largely flat-out run after Junção.
records.notes: Mercedes (uncited) supports full-speed left-hander.

records.assertion: The Café name refers to coffee's role in São Paulo regional history.
records.notes: No source in the package (cited or not) links the name to coffee history.

records.assertion: T13 is taken as a flowing sweep, not a braking point.
Turn 14 is part of the uphill run to the pit straight, associated with Subida dos Boxes.
records.notes: Mercedes (uncited) names Turn 14 itself 'Subida dos Boxes' (10% gradient).

records.assertion: Precise line matters; T14 has no established individual name.
records.notes: Implication that T14 lacks a name conflicts with Mercedes page (uncited), which calls Turn 14 'Subida dos Boxes'.

records.assertion: Turn 15 is the last numbered corner, completing the uphill sweep onto the start-finish straight.
records.notes: 15 numbered corners consistent with map and F1DB layout interlagos-2 (15 turns); uphill character not in cited sources.

records.assertion: A poor Junção exit leaves drivers vulnerable on the climb to Turn 1.
The Senna S forms the opening bends and leads downhill towards the next section.

evidence.locator: 'Where is the best place to watch?' section

records.notes: 'Next straight' implied by 'down to Turn 4', not stated.

records.assertion: The first braking zone offers overtaking; cars change direction on a descent.

evidence.locator: 'Where is the best place to watch?' section

records.assertion: A bad Senna S exit leaves the driver exposed on the following straight.
The final section climbs from the infield to the pit straight.
records.notes: 'Steeply' is not stated in the source.

records.assertion: A clean exit from the preceding left is needed to build speed uphill.
The acceleration zone decides whether an attacker can challenge at T1.
After the Senna S, Curva do Sol is a long left onto the Reta Oposta.
Curva do Sol means Curve of the Sun.
records.notes: Source oddly attributes the name to 'immense curvature'; the translation itself is supported.

records.assertion: Avoid running wide at Curva do Sol; a clean exit gains time to the next braking zone.
At the end of the Reta Oposta, cars brake for the left-hand Descida do Lago.
records.uk_issue: UK adds the translation 'Спуском до озера' here (moved from EN s2); consistent.

records.assertion: Descida do Lago means Descent to the Lake, reflecting local terrain.
records.uk_issue: UK omits the translation (it appears in UK s1 instead); says only that the name recalls the terrain.

records.assertion: Descida do Lago is a passing opportunity; overshooting the first left spoils the second.
records.notes: Source mentions a duel here but does not state it is a passing opportunity or the overshoot effect.

records.assertion: Right-hand Ferradura (Horseshoe) leads into the right-hander Laranjinha.
records.notes: 'Tightening' not stated in source.

records.assertion: These bends begin the technical infield section.
Drivers balance the car through Ferradura/Laranjinha rather than attack each apex.
Pinheirinho is a tight left followed by the tighter right-hand Bico de Pato (Duck's Bill).
records.notes: 'Even tighter' comparison not stated in source.

records.assertion: Pinheirinho and Bico de Pato force drivers to slow and change direction.
records.notes: Left-then-right sequence consistent with Mercedes page.

records.assertion: A rushed entry hampers traction on exit.
Mergulho is a fast downhill left leading to the slower left Junção.
records.notes: Downhill supported; source gives no direction for Mergulho or Junção and does not call Mergulho fast.

records.assertion: Junção is crucial because its exit starts the long uphill run to the finish line.
Giving up some entry speed at Junção pays off on the climb.
After Junção the track climbs through fast left-hand sweeps to the start-finish straight.
Subida dos Boxes means Climb to the Pits; Arquibancadas refers to grandstands.
records.notes: Source renders Arquibancadas as 'Bleachers'.

records.assertion: Drivers stay flat out from Junção to the Senna S.
